pairs.evidence: src/components/report/RecommendationTracker.tsx:69 The tracker counts every non-dismissed row as actionable and a human in_progress write carries no clock, while the only sweep in the repo (sweepExpiredLeases in src/lib/db/followup-claims.ts) requires a non-null lease, so work whose assignee has gone stays active indefinitely with no reaper.

techniques.evidence: src/lib/db/scans-recommendations.ts:88 A browser status write sets in_progress with no lease or recheck; followup-claims.ts documents this as an unleased claim with no clock and deliberately excludes it from the sweep. Last-touched is derived for the org backlog (lastActivityAt), so the free half exists, but no scheduled owner check or terminal state exists for human-held rows, and this tracker shows no last-touched.

techniques.evidence: src/lib/db/org-rollup.ts:67 The input is read here and used only to reconstruct a sample size, so the rollup never carries the value evaluateGate uses for the admission bar. This is the named failure of a rollup reporting subjects as passing that the gate blocks. The governance panel does disclose the row as not judged fleet-wide, but that text and gate.ts justify it by saying the rollup has no PR stats, which this line contradicts.

src/lib/db/org-rollup.ts:65 A missing or non-finite rate reaches the shared evaluator as null and is skipped as not measurable, which is correct for absence describing the subject's world. The separate admission-bar omission is recorded under policy-projection.
src/lib/db/org-rollup.ts:889 Could-not-run is derived from zero persisted dimensions and carried on the row, so the fleet path has a third outcome instead of reading an empty scan as a verdict.
